The Router correctly identified that eyes and nostrils are untestable due to resolution. All major structural checkpoints (head shape, fins, body) were marked present and align with the visual evidence.
artifact_review: The Router identified blur (3.5), texture anomaly (2.0), and text gibberish (1.5). The Perceptual Quality Auditor downplayed the blur/severity (score 0.4 noise), which contradicts the obvious motion blur/low-res nature of the image. I agree with the Router that the image quality is significantly degraded. The 'text_gibberish' is a critical artifact; the Image Text Auditor found no readable text, confirming the characters are nonsensical artifacts typical of AI generation or severe degradation. The background texture anomaly is also consistent with AI smoothing. The severity of the blur should be considered high as it obscures diagnostic features, but since it affects the whole image uniformly, it may be optical. However, combined with the gibberish text, it leans towards generative artifacts.
alignment_reasoning: The Fine Grained Classifier strongly confirms the class (Hammerhead Shark) with high confidence (logit 7.82 vs 1.71 for next best). Visually, the distinctive cephalofoil, dorsal fin, and caudal fin are present and structurally correct. 6 out of 10 checkpoints were testable and passed. The 4 untestable checkpoints were due to resolution limits, not absence of features. The image conforms well to the class taxonomy despite low fidelity.
artifact_reasoning: Significant artifacts are present. 1) Text Gibberish: The timestamp in the corner is illegible/nonsensical, a strong AI indicator. 2) Texture Anomaly: The sandy background lacks granular detail, appearing smeared/painterly. 3) Blur/Noise: The entire image suffers from heavy blur and noise, reducing clarity. While some blur could be optical, the combination with text failure and background smoothing suggests generative origin or severe compression. The artifact score is penalized heavily for the text and texture issues, but not catastrophically low because the subject itself is coherent and not melted.
